faded-charcoal.$description: Faded Charcoal — Primary text, headings, icons, borders, prominent interactive elements. It's the dominant dark shade, appearing in place of true black.

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Page backgrounds, card surfaces, primary light background. Provides a soft, warm canvas contrasting with Faded Charcoal.

soft-gray.$description: Soft Gray — Subtle borders, inactive elements, muted backgrounds. A pale, desaturated gray for separation without harshness.

light-peach.$description: Light Peach — Occasional background accents, footer background, illustration fills. A very pale, warm background hint.

subtle-ash.$description: Subtle Ash — Secondary text, descriptive elements, subdued icons. Provides hierarchy without being too light.

true-black.$description: True Black — System icons, some text elements. Used sparingly, mostly for icon rendering or specific high-contrast text.

dusty-sage.$description: Dusty Sage — Tertiary text, subtle icon detailing. Further de-emphasizes content.

action-red.$description: Action Red — Primary call-to-action buttons, active navigation indicators, key interactive elements. This vivid red stands out against the muted palette.

link-orange.$description: Link Orange — Inline links, slightly darker shade of brand red used for text.

accent-blue.$description: Accent Blue — Secondary links, distinct interactive elements. A cool counterpoint to the dominant red.

teal-accent.$description: Teal Accent — Specific illustrative text or decorative elements. A muted teal that occasionally appears as an accent.

success-green.$description: Success Green — Success states, specific informational badges. A moderate green for positive affirmation.

badge-green.$description: Badge Green — Text color for specific badges, slightly darker than Success Green.

light-green-tint.$description: Light Green Tint — Background for success badges. A very light, near-gray green.

graphik.$description: Primary display and heading font. Used for prominent titles and key marketing messages. The slight tightening of letter spacing at larger sizes gives it a refined, bespoke feel, avoiding the sprawl of default sans-serifs.

inter.$description: Primary body font, UI elements, buttons, links, and forms. Its wide range of weights and subtle tracking variations ensure readability and visual hierarchy across all transactional and informational content.

arial.$description: Fallback font for specific input elements, indicating utilitarian use where broad system compatibility is prioritized over specific branding.

caecilia.$description: Used for specific body text sections, particularly for testimonials or quotes. Its serif nature provides a distinct, classic, and editorial feel, breaking the sans-serif dominance.

shantell-sans.$description: Rarely used, possibly for decorative or illustrative text. Its distinct, informal style provides a whimsical contrast to the otherwise structured design.
